description: Shared Renovate policy for millsymills-com and millsmillsymills. Extend it from a repo with {"extends": ["local>millsymills-com/.github:renovate-config"]} inside the org, or {"extends": ["github>millsymills-com/.github:renovate-config"]} from the user account.
Rationale, measurements, and the automerge boundary are in millsymills-com/millsymills-com-org docs/adr/0007-renovate-over-dependabot.md. Change the policy here, not per repo.

Delete a repo's .github/dependabot.yml when you onboard it. Two bots on one manifest means duplicate PRs and races on the same lockfile. Dependabot *alerts* stay on — they are declared in tofu and Renovate reads them.

Automerge here only takes effect where a repo has at least one required status check. GitHub offers auto-merge only on a pull request that cannot already be merged, so on a repo with no required check platformAutomerge silently no-ops.

Advisory-driven updates skip both the cooldown and the twice-weekly window, because for a known-exploitable version the delay is the risk. Schedule immunity comes from this object's default empty schedule, so no schedule key is set here — writing one would overwrite that default and re-impose the window.

They do not skip the human: the 7-day cooldown exists because a freshly published version is when a compromised release is most likely to still be live, so waiving it and the reviewer at once would drop both defenses in the same step.

Refresh transitive pins that no manifest edit would touch (`uv lock --upgrade`, and the equivalent per manager). Twice a month rather than once, so a missed run costs half a month instead of a whole one.

This is automerged and is a deliberate carve-out from the majors rule: lockFileMaintenance is its own updateType, so the major rule does not match it and a transitive dependency can cross a major inside one of these PRs. It is accepted because the change is confined to the lockfile, no manifest constraint moves, and the repo's required checks are the gate.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. A grouped merge once carried docker/metadata-action v5 to v6 with nobody reading the changelog; majors get their own PR and a deliberate look. addLabels, not labels, so a later matching rule cannot drop the marker.
Never bump the interpreter floor. Raising requires-python is a support decision, not a dependency update.
Python dev and build tooling. Covers both layouts in use: [project.optional-dependencies] (unifi-mcp, unraid-mcp) and [dependency-groups] (consistency-check).
Python runtime dependencies. Kept out of the dev group so a shipped bump is never hidden behind a test-only one — the split unifi-mcp, unraid-mcp, and gandi-mcp already made by hand.
requirements.txt repos have no manifest depTypes to split on, so they group as one.

GitHub Actions. helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests keeps the SHA-pin-with-version-comment shape the workflow convention requires. millsymills-com-org overrides this to false in its own renovate.json — an actions bump there trips gate-verified and cannot clear it.

Go modules are grouped but not automerged. The one Go repo in the fleet gates on a single `test` check, which is too thin to land a dependency bump unattended. Flip this to true once it also runs vet and a linter.

Terraform providers and the tflint plugins. Scoped to the provider depTypes because the terraform manager emits two dozen, most of which are not providers. Grouped for minor and patch only — a provider major must not arrive bundled with routine bumps, which is the shape that caused the metadata-action incident. Never automerged: a provider bump reaches every repo in the org through tofu-apply, and the plan output is the review.

Astral tools move fast at 0.x and a minor there can change lint or type behavior. Still automerged — the failure mode is a red lint or type check on the PR, which blocks the merge rather than landing it. Names are matched as packageName, so the pre-commit hook repos are listed separately from the PyPI distributions.
